sources.name: InterNACHI Home Inspection Standards of Practice
ASHI Standard of Practice for Home Inspections

checks: Roof covering (shingles, tile, metal, flat membrane), viewed from the roof, the eaves or the ground
Gutters and downspouts
Flashing, vents, skylights, chimney and other penetrations
Roof structure from accessible attic areas
defects: Missing, curled, cracked or granule-worn shingles
Lifted or rusted flashing at walls and chimneys
Active leaks or stains below the roof
Gutters pulled loose or draining against the foundation
scope: Walking an unsafe or fragile roof
Predicting how many years the roof has left
Water testing or certifying the roof

checks: Insulation type and approximate depth
Ventilation of the attic space
Bath, kitchen and laundry exhaust fans and where they vent
Visible roof framing and sheathing
defects: Thin or missing insulation
Fans venting into the attic instead of outside
Staining or mold-like growth on sheathing from poor ventilation
Signs of rodents or pests
scope: Entering an attic that is not safely accessible
Determining R-value or whether ventilation is adequate

checks: Siding, trim, eaves, soffits and fascia
Exterior doors and a representative number of windows
Decks, porches, balconies, stairs, railings and guards
Grading, drainage, walkways, driveways and retaining walls where they affect the house
defects: Wood rot at trim and door frames
Loose deck ledgers, wobbly railings, unsafe baluster spacing
Negative grading sending water toward the foundation
Cracked stucco or siding gaps letting water in

checks: Foundation type and visible condition
Basement and crawlspace, where accessible
Visible structural framing: joists, beams, posts
Signs of water entry and movement
defects: Cracks, bowing walls or displacement
Water staining, efflorescence or standing water
Wood touching soil, rot or insect damage
Cut or notched joists
scope: Entering a crawlspace that is unsafe or too tight
Moving stored items to see walls and floors

checks: Service drop, meter, service-entrance conductors and main disconnect
Panelboards and breakers or fuses
Grounding and bonding
A representative number of outlets, switches and fixtures; GFCI and AFCI devices
Presence of smoke and carbon monoxide alarms
defects: Double-tapped breakers and open panel slots
Missing GFCI protection near water
Reversed polarity or ungrounded outlets
Solid-conductor aluminum branch wiring
Missing smoke or CO alarms
scope: Low-voltage wiring, security, phone and data systems
Testing smoke alarms or resetting breakers

checks: Main water and fuel shut-off valves
Water heater, venting and TPR valve
Supply flow at fixtures, toilets, drains and visible drain-waste-vent piping
Sump pumps with accessible floats
defects: Active leaks under sinks and at toilets
Low flow with two fixtures running
Missing or improper TPR discharge pipe
Slow drains and loose toilets
scope: Septic systems and sewer lines under the yard

checks: Heating system operation from the thermostat
Cooling system operation from the thermostat
Energy source, method and thermostat location
Visible venting, filters and ductwork
defects: System does not respond to the thermostat
Rusted or improperly vented gas appliances
Dirty filters and condensate leaks
Equipment near or past typical service life (noted, not a defect on its own)
scope: Sizing, BTU capacity and airflow balance

checks: Floors, walls and ceilings
A representative number of doors and windows
Stairs, railings and guards
Fireplace: visible firebox, damper, hearth and lintel
defects: Ceiling stains from roof or plumbing leaks
Fogged double-pane windows (failed seals)
Loose handrails and wide baluster gaps
Missing smoke or CO alarm in a room with a fireplace

checks: Garage vehicle doors and openers
Auto-reverse and photo-eye safety sensors
Fire separation between the garage and the house
Slab, walls and visible framing
defects: Opener that does not reverse or sensors out of alignment
Non-fire-rated door into the house
Holes in the fire-separation wall
Slab cracks with water entry
